_note: REVISION 2: positions recalculated using the correct method the user pointed out. Every numbered box on the official map has a thin BLACK LINE running from the box to the real street — it is the point where that line touches the street (not the position of the box itself, and not colour alone) that marks the exact stand location. The box/street colour is only a rough indicator (the map often also tints the street segment associated with that borgo), never proof on its own. Method used for this revision: for each borgo, (1) visually traced the black line from the box to its point of contact with the street, on high-resolution crops of the original image (4125x2820px), (2) checked whether the street segment at that point is tinted the same colour as the borgo (colour-street correlation), (3) checked consistency of distance/position relative to neighbouring borghi and the street names visible on the map, (4) for borgo 5, applied the user's explicit correction directly (Via Boccaccio, not Corso Verdi), then used it as an anchor to calibrate the others. A second, independent method (an automated dark-pixel column scan tracing each line) was used as a cross-check where available and agrees within 2-4 percentage points for most borghi. confidence: 'high' = line/colour clearly traced and agreeing across both methods; 'medium' = a plausible line but neighbouring boxes close together or automated tracing absent/disagreeing, to be confirmed on site; all positions remain a map-based estimate, not a GPS survey.
